project.name: kiln
project.description: Kiln is an evidence-backed decision research system for applied AI and LLM engineering, covering serving, RAG, agents, evaluation, and fine-tune versus retrieval tradeoffs. It pairs a LangGraph research agent with a NestJS job API, a React dashboard, and a curated docs corpus.

nodes.languageNotes: Each job pins its toolchain version and uses a per-job defaults.run.working-directory so the monorepo apps build independently without a workspace-level orchestrator.

nodes.name: 001_research_lifecycle_owner.sql
nodes.summary: First Postgres migration that gives research runs an execution-ownership lifecycle: it adds execution/version, job, timing and heartbeat columns to research_runs, adds execution/attempt/sequence ordering columns to run_events, and introduces the research_dispatch_outbox table for transactional job dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT and written entirely with IF NOT EXISTS guards, so the migration is idempotent and safe to re-run by the compose migrate service.

nodes.name: research_dispatch_outbox
nodes.summary: Transactional outbox table holding pending research job dispatches, keyed to a run and its execution version, with payload, attempt counter and dispatched_at marker plus a partial index over undispatched rows.

nodes.name: 002_knowledge_corpus.sql
nodes.summary: Second Postgres migration that provisions the reusable knowledge and corpus layer: it creates knowledge_records for cached cited answers, corpus_documents for chunked and embedded evidence, and corpus_sync_runs for tracking indexing generations, then backfills extra columns and indexes on each.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a create-then-ALTER ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS style so the same file can both initialise a fresh database and incrementally upgrade one created by an earlier schema version.

nodes.name: knowledge_records
nodes.summary: Stores reusable research answers with their citations, embedding and embedding model, plus fingerprint/query arrays, depth score, reuse counters and status used to decide when a past run can be replayed instead of re-researched.

nodes.name: corpus_documents
nodes.summary: Holds retrievable evidence chunks with source url, host, tier, quote and credibility score, plus source_path/chunk_index provenance and generation/active flags that support atomic corpus re-indexing.
nodes.languageNotes: The unique index on (source_path, chunk_index) makes re-ingesting a corpus file an upsert rather than a duplicate insert.

nodes.name: corpus_sync_runs
nodes.summary: Audit table recording each corpus indexing run with its status, generation number, source hash, document counts, embedding model and error text, so partially failed syncs can be detected and retried.

nodes.name: 003_tenancy.sql
nodes.summary: Third Postgres migration introducing multi-tenant org and user tables, membership roles, run sharing, usage ledger, notifications, and org API keys; it backfills org_id on research_runs, scenarios, and knowledge_records and seeds a default organization.
nodes.languageNotes: Seeds org_default and records the migration in schema_migrations; all tenancy columns use IF NOT EXISTS so the file is safe on partially migrated databases.

nodes.name: schema_migrations
nodes.summary: Migration ledger recording which numbered SQL migrations have been applied and when.

nodes.name: organizations
nodes.summary: Tenant organization with plan, monthly run quota, retention policy, and Stripe billing identifiers.

nodes.name: users
nodes.summary: Application user profile keyed by external auth id with optional email, name, and avatar URL.

nodes.name: memberships
nodes.summary: Many-to-many join between organizations and users with a role string defaulting to org:member.

nodes.name: run_shares
nodes.summary: Shareable read tokens for research runs scoped to an organization with optional expiry and revocation.

nodes.name: usage_ledger
nodes.summary: Append-only usage events per organization tracking token counts and estimated cost for billing analytics.

nodes.name: notifications
nodes.summary: In-app notifications for org members tied to runs with read/unread state.

nodes.name: org_api_keys
nodes.summary: Hashed organization API keys with scoped permissions, prefix for lookup, and revocation support.

nodes.name: product_events
nodes.summary: Lightweight product analytics events with optional org and user attribution stored as JSON props.

nodes.name: 004_evidence_graph.sql
nodes.summary: Fourth Postgres migration defining the evidence graph for citation verification: research_sources, research_spans, research_claims, and research_claim_edges link runs to quoted spans and supporting sources.
nodes.languageNotes: Enforces UNIQUE (run_id, url) on sources and UNIQUE (run_id, claim_key) on claims so hover locators stay stable across report revisions.

nodes.name: research_sources
nodes.summary: Fetched source documents for a research run with url, tier, quality band, content hash and full text for grounding.

nodes.name: research_spans

nodes.summary: Fifth Postgres migration adding parent_run_id to research_runs so follow-up research threads can reference the originating run, with a partial index over active child runs.

nodes.name: 01_rag_hybrid_vs_vectors.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note arguing that RAG does not require a vector database, since BM25 and hybrid retrieval often match dense-only stacks on small or identifier-heavy corpora. Ingested by the agent's retrieval layer as a peer-reviewed-tier source.
nodes.languageNotes: Every corpus file shares the same front-matter block (Source / URL / Published / Credibility) under an H1 heading, which the ingestion pipeline parses into document metadata and credibility tiers.

nodes.name: 02_agent_loops_vs_pipelines.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note distinguishing true agent loops (conditional edges, critic loop-back, budgets, HITL interrupts, durable checkpoints) from linear pipelines drawn as graphs. Sourced from LangGraph orchestration documentation.

nodes.name: 03_vllm_serving_batching.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on vLLM serving mechanics: PagedAttention KV cache, continuous batching, prefix caching, and the throughput versus time-to-first-token tradeoff under load.

nodes.name: 04_llm_as_judge_bias.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on evaluation methodology, warning that LLM-as-judge inherits position, verbosity, and self-preference bias and should screen rather than replace human-labeled golden sets.

nodes.name: 05_finetune_vs_rag_vs_context.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note comparing fine-tuning, RAG, and long context for injecting new facts, recommending RAG for volatile facts, light SFT/DPO for format, and long context for retrieved packs.

nodes.name: 06_tool_calling_reliability.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on tool-calling reliability, explaining that constrained decoding fixes format but not tool or argument choice, and that retries, schema validation, and idempotent tools matter more than model swaps.

nodes.name: 07_observability_cost.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on per-node tracing and cost attribution for research agents, covering token accounting, planner/critic/report cost splits, and the need for durable run events to debug loops and HITL.

nodes.name: 08_benchmark_caveats.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on benchmark caveats (MMLU contamination, SWE-bench harness specificity, leaderboard scaffolding), arguing that a domain golden set should be the ship gate.

nodes.name: 09_multiagent_myths.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note challenging multi-agent superiority claims, noting coordination cost and context duplication, and stating that Kiln's critic loop is a single role-based graph rather than a swarm.

nodes.name: 10_prompt_injection.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note treating prompt injection as a product-level risk, recommending fetch-host allowlists, delimited evidence channels, HITL for high-privilege tools, and adversarial corpus pages in evals.

nodes.name: 11_quantization_quality.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on quantization tradeoffs, explaining how INT4/AWQ/GPTQ and FP8 raise concurrency while task-level quality deltas on tool calling and long RAG packs require per-precision product evals.

nodes.name: 12_embeddings_rerank.md
nodes.summary: Corpus evidence note on retrieval quality mechanics: chunk size and overlap dominate embedding choice, and a cheap first-stage retriever plus cross-encoder rerank is the standard quality jump.

nodes.name: agent-research-system.md
nodes.summary: Architecture guide for the Kiln research agent: budgeted LangGraph pipeline with briefing, planner, parallel search/scholar/docs collectors, critic gate, HITL interrupts, and report composition. Explains the four-layer separation (boundary, graph nodes, domain rules, adapters), state-as-bus design, and the Nest-to-agent request path.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what Kiln is: evidence-backed decision research for applied AI/LLM systems. The document maps five product surfaces (Research, Scenarios, Corpus, Workspace, Settings), shows the LangGraph research loop as an ASCII diagram, and lists the Python agent, NestJS API, React UI, Postgres, and Qdrant stack. Treat this as the roadmap for everything that follows.

tour.title: Agent Architecture Guide
tour.description: Building on the README overview, read docs/agent-research-system.md for the four-layer agent design: boundary (FastAPI), graph nodes, domain rules, and adapters. It explains the budgeted pipeline—briefing, planner, parallel collectors, critic loop-back, HITL interrupts, and report composition—and how the NestJS API submits work to the Python agent. Pair this mental model with graph/builder.py, which wires those nodes and conditional edges into a compiled LangGraph.

tour.title: Agent Runtime Entry
tour.description: The Python service boots from main.py, a FastAPI app exposing health checks, streaming execution, corpus ingestion, and knowledge endpoints. runtime.py is the execution heart: it initializes LangGraph, streams Server-Sent Event frames to callers, resumes from checkpoints after HITL pauses, and annotates progress. Together they form the boundary between the NestJS job API and the research graph.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI uses dependency injection and async route handlers; LangGraph checkpoints let long-running agent loops pause for human input and resume without losing state.

tour.title: Graph State & Assembly
tour.description: graph/state.py defines ResearchState, the TypedDict bus every node reads and writes—budget counters, evidence slots, critic signals, and memo drafts. builder.py imports all node callables and registers conditional routes (for example, critic loop-back versus proceed to report). domain/schema.py supplies the Pydantic models behind that state and is the most imported file in the codebase, making it the shared vocabulary of the pipeline.

tour.title: Research Loop Nodes
tour.description: The graph nodes implement each research phase. planner.py decomposes the goal into sub-queries and retrieval plans; search.py and scholar.py fetch web and academic evidence; critic.py evaluates coverage slots and claim confidence, routing back for enrichment or forward to HITL; hitl.py pauses for human resume decisions; report.py triggers memo composition. Follow these files to see how conditional edges turn a linear pipeline into a true agent loop with budgets and checkpoints.

tour.title: Evidence & Citations
tour.description: Domain rules keep memos grounded. coverage.py scores must-answer slots and builds evidence dossiers; citations.py normalizes URLs, validates tiers, and builds inline citation ledgers; hybrid retrieval in retrieval/hybrid.py combines dense embeddings with BM25 lexical scoring. These modules sit between raw fetch results and the report writer, enforcing the evidence-backed standard Kiln promises in its README.

tour.title: Memo Composition
tour.description: When the graph reaches the report node, report/compose.py assembles markdown sections, adversarial tables, and numbered citations from graph state. deep_write.py adds ODR-style long-form generation with depth-aware LLM budgets. report_integrity.py and report_audit.py run deterministic post-write checks for unsupported claims and structural issues before the memo is published back through the API.

tour.title: NestJS Job API
tour.description: The NestJS layer orchestrates product concerns around the agent. research.controller.ts exposes REST endpoints to start, resume, and share runs; research.service.ts coordinates auth, billing, and dispatch; research.processor.ts is the BullMQ worker that calls agent-execution.client.ts to stream results from the Python service; research.repository.ts persists runs, events, and memos in Postgres. packages/contracts/src/index.ts defines the shared Zod schemas both API and web import.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS modules group controllers, services, and Bull queue processors; BullMQ decouples HTTP request acceptance from long-running agent execution.

tour.title: React Dashboard Entry
tour.description: The web client mounts from main.tsx and App.tsx, wiring Clerk authentication, client-side routing, and the Shell layout. Research.tsx is the primary workspace: it starts runs, opens SSE progress streams via lib/api.ts, and renders the live memo with evidence panels. lib/sse.ts handles authenticated streaming so users see graph progress without polling.

tour.title: Memo Presentation UI
tour.description: Once a run completes, presentation components turn agent output into a readable decision brief. MemoMarkdown.tsx renders KaTeX math, citation tokens, ASCII diagrams, and lazy Mermaid blocks; DecisionCard.tsx surfaces the recommendation with prose cleanup; Share.tsx provides a public read-only view with sources. These components consume the same memo shape the agent composes in Step 7, closing the loop from graph state to user-facing output.

tour.title: Data & Deployment
tour.description: Postgres tables anchor persistence: research_runs tracks lifecycle and execution ownership, while knowledge_records and corpus_documents (from migrations 002) store reusable answers and retrievable evidence chunks. docker-compose.yml orchestrates Postgres, Redis, Qdrant, the agent, API, and nginx-served web UI for local and Oracle deployments. render.yaml and .github/workflows/ci.yml define production Blueprint hosting and the three-job CI pipeline that tests agent, API, and web on every push.
tour.languageLesson: docker-compose service depends_on with healthchecks ensures migrations finish before the API starts; Render Blueprint env var references wire managed Postgres into both agent and API services.
